description: ASTRA is a team of passionate students and innovators using artificial intelligence, data science, and software development to solve real-world challenges. By leveraging NASA’s open data, we develop creative, data-driven solutions related to Earth and space. Driven by curiosity, collaboration, and innovation, we aim to transform scientific knowledge into meaningful impact.
summary:
ASTRA-SN is an interactive decision-support platform designed to help users explore and assess potential landing sites in the Lunar South Pole region.

The platform brings together terrain visualization, solar illumination analysis, and Earth visibility assessment in one environment. Users can explore lunar terrain in 3D, select a location and analysis period, examine how sunlight and Earth visibility evolve over time, and compare different locations.

By making lunar environmental information easier to explore and interpret, ASTRA-SN addresses a key challenge in future lunar missions: understanding not only where a lander could operate, but also when environmental conditions may be favorable for energy availability and communication.

Our goal is to make complex lunar data more accessible and support more informed preliminary landing-site assessment.
details:
ASTRA-SN is an interactive lunar exploration and decision-support platform focused on the Lunar South Pole. It was developed in response to the NASA Space Apps Challenge's Lunar Landing Site Navigator challenge, which highlights the need to understand the environmental conditions that influence lunar landing-site selection and mission operations.

The project addresses a major difficulty in lunar exploration: although decades of space missions have generated extensive scientific data, relevant information remains distributed across different datasets and specialized tools. ASTRA-SN aims to make these resources easier to explore and interpret through a unified interface.

How It Works

The platform focuses on three major aspects of lunar site assessment:

1. Terrain and Elevation

Users can explore the lunar South Pole through interactive 3D terrain visualization. This helps them understand the surface configuration and identify surrounding terrain features that may influence visibility.

2. Solar Illumination

ASTRA-SN allows users to configure an analysis period and examine the visibility of the Sun from a selected location. By accounting for the local terrain horizon, the platform helps identify periods of illumination and shadow.

This is particularly relevant for lunar landers and equipment that depend on solar energy.

3. Earth Visibility and Communication

The platform also evaluates the visibility of Earth from a selected location. This helps identify periods when a direct line of sight may be available, providing useful information for preliminary communication-window assessment.

Users can visualize how these conditions evolve over time through a timeline and compare different locations.

Technology and Methodology

ASTRA-SN combines lunar terrain information, astronomical position calculations, and interactive visualization.

The project uses NASA lunar exploration resources, including data and products associated with the Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter and its LOLA instrument. Astronomy Engine is used for celestial position calculations.

The platform brings these elements together so that users can explore a location, configure an analysis period, examine illumination and Earth visibility, and compare results without constantly switching between different tools.

Technology stack:

  • Frontend: React 19, TypeScript, Vite, React Router, Zustand, and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend and engine: Python; FastAPI and Uvicorn provide the API. The scientific engine uses astronomy-engine, NumPy, SciPy, Rasterio, and PyProj.
  • Languages: TypeScript and Python primarily, with some JavaScript for tooling.
  • Visualization: Three.js with React Three Fiber and Drei for 3D lunar views; Recharts for charts and timelines.
  • Other technologies: Framer Motion for animation, Lucide React for icons, Docker for the API, and Vercel for hosting the static frontend. NASA LOLA terrain data feeds the terrain analysis.

Benefits and Intended Impact

ASTRA-SN is intended to support preliminary lunar landing-site assessment by making environmental information more accessible and easier to interpret.

Its potential users include mission planners, researchers, educators, students, and space enthusiasts.

By combining terrain exploration, illumination analysis, Earth visibility, and temporal visualization, the platform can help users better understand the relationship between location, terrain, and time when studying potential lunar landing sites.

Beyond mission-planning applications, ASTRA-SN also aims to make lunar science more accessible to people who may not have specialized knowledge of planetary science.

Creativity and Design Considerations

The creative aspect of ASTRA-SN lies in bringing several complementary dimensions of lunar site assessment into one interactive environment.

Rather than presenting isolated datasets, the platform allows users to explore how terrain, sunlight, and Earth visibility relate to one another and change over time.

During development, we considered the importance of terrain geometry, changing illumination conditions, potential communication windows, data availability, and the need to make complex scientific information understandable through an accessible interface.

ASTRA-SN is currently focused on the Lunar South Pole and is designed as an evolving project. Future improvements include expanding coverage to the Lunar North Pole, integrating additional datasets, improving the user experience, and developing a fully operational AI assistant.
